objectClass.primaryType: open-air medieval cloth-dyeing rack with two heated banded vats
objectClass.notes: Three cloth colors, two readable dye vats and the wringer must remain separate; no flat banner wall may substitute for draped textiles.

reasoning: The broad post-and-beam silhouette is interrupted by three hanging cloth masses, two vats, a wringer and a foreground tool cluster.
Cloth must show gravity sag, fold depth, hems and wet/dry material contrast rather than planar cards.
The heated vat requires supported legs, stone fire ring, ash, liquid and a safe contact hierarchy.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required by draped cloth geometry, banded vats, wringer mechanics, fire foundation and mixed-fiber tool cluster.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Back-side rack joints are inferred from the symmetrical post-and-beam construction.
Dye liquids are restrained reflective surfaces and not simulated fluids.

details.description: Two heavy posts, base shoes and paired top beams use pegged joints, rounded wear and projected end grain.
Multiple rope collars bind the main posts and display twisted strand relief.
Diagonal knee braces and projecting round pegs lock the upper rack and create small silhouette breaks.
Indigo wool hangs in a broad U-shaped double layer with irregular vertical folds and a frayed hem.
Madder-red cloth has deeper asymmetric folds, a lower staggered hem and a visible secondary layer.
Saffron cloth forms a narrower drape with softened folds and frayed lower corners.
Dry wool uses coarse woven normal relief, matte cavities and slightly polished fold crests.
The left vat uses individual tapered staves, three iron hoops, side handles, four feet and a deep projected rim.
The right vat repeats the stave-and-hoop system at a distinct size beneath the wringer.
Indigo and madder liquids show low-roughness dark surfaces, wet rims and color-matched downward drips.
A long wooden paddle embeds into the indigo liquid and leans against the vat rim without floating.
Two supported posts carry a horizontal roller, crank handle and dripping folded wet cloth above the madder vat.
Irregular fieldstones form a complete fire ring with dark ash, charred supports and restrained embers beneath the indigo vat.
A wicker basket uses interlaced vertical ribs and horizontal weave around folded cream cloth with deep folds.
Four earthenware jars and a pigment bowl use separate profiles, colored residues and grouped placement beside a rope coil.

anatomy.note: Object domain; character anatomy is not applicable.

definitionOfDone: Three dimensional cloth masses, two functioning banded vats, wringer mechanics, heated foundation and fiber/ceramic tools remain legible from main and side views with distinct wet and dry material response.

qualityCriteria: Post shoes, posts, braces, beams, pegs and lashings form a credible supported rack.
Indigo, madder and saffron cloths have gravity folds, thickness, separate hems and clear spacing.
Both stave vats, liquids, hoops, handles and the stone fire foundation remain readable.
Roller, crank, wet cloth, paddle, basket, jars and rope are supported and visible.
Dry wool, wet cloth, liquid dye, oak, iron, wicker, ceramic, stone and ash respond independently.

antiShallowSpecRules: Flat rectangular cloth cards may not pass.
The two vats may not merge into generic cylinders.
The wringer may not float above the vat.
Dye liquid may not be opaque flat paint.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from the admitted reference before implementation.
